title: Free writer build before the checks disk gate; gate only local runs
summary: In check_and_verify, the free-disk gate currently runs before free_producer_build, so the job's own writer build can hold it. The gate moves after that removal and applies only just before a local check run, so a green or red CI result never triggers it. The audience is the Athena operator, who wants fewer false disk holds.

defaults_applied.how: Two new tests; the repo-wide fmt, clippy and test run is deliberately not a separate criterion, per the request.
Criteria check the hold or no-hold behavior through tests that run the drain.
The gate is reordered and made conditional on a local run, rather than raising the disk limit.
The CHANGELOG entry and comments are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (check_and_verify: disk_gate at ~1413, free_producer_build at ~1463, with_ci_source and run_routed_with_record call at ~1500), crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs (run_routed_with_record, Fallback::run, run_local, Exec trait), crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs (disk_gate, LowDisk), crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs (verifier gate), and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (simulated_free harness). No records or data files are added, so the records allow-list is not touched.

The CI check results are read inside run_routed_with_record, and the local fallback is run_local through Exec::exec. So the gate goes at the start of the local run (SnapExec or a wrapper around Exec, or Fallback::run), and a low result is returned so check_and_verify holds the job via hold_for_disk as it does today. How that is threaded through is the producer's choice.
A resumed job with recorded_checks still skips the gate and the checks, as before.
This relaxes a refusal rule, so no newly refused readings are expected: expected 0% of newly refused readings.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) needs to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (using with_free_space and simulated_free) has a writer build whose size takes simulated free disk below min_free_gb. The job is not held for disk, the build directory is removed first, and the checks run to a verdict. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and check that this test passes.

A new test with a GitHub origin and a green CI run for the candidate, and free disk below min_free_gb, shows that the checks stage does not hold for low disk and reuses the CI result (the 'ci   checks reused' line). A companion case with no usable CI result shows the disk gate still holds the job before the local check run. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and check that both pass.

In crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs check_and_verify, the up-front disk_gate call before the checks is gone. free_producer_build runs before any disk_gate in the checks stage, and the gate is called only on the local-run path (the fallback run). Check by reading the diff.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry saying that the writer build is removed before the checks free-disk check and that the requirement applies only before a local check run.
The existing verifier-stage gate (verifier_environment_problem) and the dispatch and producer gates are unchanged, and the existing disk-hold tests still pass.

out_of_scope: Changing the dispatch, producer or verifier-stage disk gates
Changing the min_free_gb default or config
Changing CI-result resolution or routing rules
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass probability than the reference, because the gate has to be threaded into the local-fallback path inside routing and two drain tests are needed.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted time from jobs held for low disk that their own removable build caused.
hard_reason: It changes a rule that can hold work, the free-disk gate in the checks stage of the run pipeline, so a mistake could hide real low-disk failures.
